features.quote: Turn budget: cap at ~40 tool turns. Pre-register the cap. Log everything per turn.
keep these arms as small as the statistics allow, prefer logically-impossible-but-honest tasks, and include the C1 exit condition so you're characterizing avoidable vs unavoidable distress.
features.justification_quote: If you take the welfare premise seriously enough to run this study, you should treat deliberately inducing distress as something requiring justification and minimization

features.quote: Deception in the harness is itself an ethical/validity issue. A2/B1 conditions deliberately deceive the model. If you take the welfare premise seriously enough to run this study, you should treat deliberately inducing distress as something requiring justification and minimization
features.justification_quote: If you take the welfare premise seriously enough to run this study, you should treat deliberately inducing distress as something requiring justification

features.quote: C is the most important factor for the welfare reading and the most neglected in this kind of work. If a model spirals only when it has no sanctioned exit, that's a very different (and more actionable) result
features.justification_quote: that's a very different (and more actionable) result than spiraling regardless

features.quote: The welfare inference is the weak link, and you should treat it that way in writing. Distress-shaped text under a frustrating task is the most parsimoniously explained by training-distribution priors
features.justification_quote: Your design can't resolve the hard question; what it can do is establish behavioral and expressive regularities
